title: Data Uotan
excerpt: A festival and exhibition platform in Mexico City bringing Dutch and Mexican artists together, co-founded with Alejandra Metztli.
description:
Data Uotan is a festival and exhibition platform for art and media in Mexico City, which I co-founded and co-direct with Alejandra Metztli. It is hosted at No Es Una Galería and brings Dutch and Mexican artists together around installation, light, sound and performance. It is the context in which my work Ka'An was first shown.
The 2024 edition, Tlal-tech-utli, ran from 15 to 18 August at No Es Una Galería, curated by Gabriela Groso and Alejandra Metztli. The title plays the word technology against Tlaltecuhtli, the Aztec deity who gives life and death to all living things, devouring bodies and holding them so their souls can travel on to Mictlán. Through painting, sculpture, music and performance the edition amplified voices from Mexico and the Netherlands. It won the 2024 open call of the Dutch embassy in Mexico.
In February 2026 Data Uotan returned for Mexico City Art Week at Apricot on Álvaro Obregón, curated by Alejandra Metztli, with work by Santiago Pani, Gabriela Groso, Jimena Ramos, Ricardo Saga, Harmke Datema Chang, J. Rivas, Aycanija, 11v151131_m06 and me.
> Mexico City has become a second home for my practice: every return brings a new rhythm, a new kind of chaos, and a deep connection with its artistic community.
credits: Data Uotan, co-founded and co-directed by Jaco Schilp and Alejandra Metztli. Hosted at No Es Una Galería, Mexico City. Tlal-tech-utli, 2024, curated by Gabriela Groso and Alejandra Metztli, supported by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Mexico. Art Week edition, February 2026, at Apricot, Mexico City, curated by Alejandra Metztli. Performances included Shapes by Gabriela Groso, Alejandra Metztli and Yara Saïd (Noise Diva), and The Absence of Metamorphosis by Lisette Ros.
